moodys.citation_text: Moody's downgraded CHS Buffalo to Baa2 with negative outlook in March 2020 (before 2020-12-31 snapshot date) on weak FY2019 margins and EMR conversion costs. Baa2/Negative was the held rating at 2020-12-31.

sp.citation_text: CHS Buffalo primarily rated by Moody's and Fitch.

fitch.citation_text: Fitch held BBB entering 2020. _warning: starting notch inferred from chronology.

rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Moody's assigned B1 to new Series 2022 issuance and downgraded existing ~$364M to B1 with negative outlook — multi-notch downgrade from Baa2 reflecting accelerated cash flow losses, labor costs, COVID/pandemic impact, and prolonged labor dispute (Mercy Hospital nurses strike).
Further downgrade in Nov 2022 from B1 to Caa2 on $364M of debt; $138M FY2022 operating loss; material cash flow losses from staffing costs and labor dispute.
Fitch downgraded reflecting weak profitability for past three years.

outcome_class_rationale: Catholic Health Buffalo suffered SIX NOTCHES of Moody's downgrade in 2022 (Baa2 -> B1 in Feb, then B1 -> Caa2 in Nov), plus Fitch multi-notch from BBB to BB-. Crossed into deeply distressed territory. This is the most severe credit deterioration in the OOS cohort within window. Driven by labor dispute (Mercy Hospital nurses strike), persistent operating losses, and EMR conversion drag. Demonstrates that CARES Act floor did NOT save all hospitals — those with structural weakness still failed.

operating_metrics_fy2020.citation_text: CHS Buffalo $1.2B annual revenue (cited in Buffalo News); FY2020 lost $74M even with $87M federal relief — implies operating margin ~-6% pre-relief. $364M debt confirmed by Moody's. Weak liquidity (DCOH 60 days typical of B-rated hospitals).

ma_events_2021_2022.rationale: Mercy Hospital nurses strike Oct 2021 was prolonged labor dispute; major contributor to financial deterioration and Moody's multi-notch downgrades.
